verses.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचअनाश्रितः कर्मफलं कार्यं कर्म करोति यः । स संन्यासी च योगी च न निरग्निर्न चाक्रियः ॥
verses.tr: One who performs the required action without taking shelter in the fruit of action is a renunciate and a yogi. Not one who merely gives up fire, and not one who merely stops acting.
verses.angle: Yogi is one who acts without leaning on fruit
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna begins by redefining what a renunciate and a yogi truly are. Listen to how he describes the inner state of the one who acts.

body.text: One who performs the required action without taking shelter in the fruit of action is a renunciate and a yogi. Not one who merely gives up fire, and not one who merely stops acting. Krishna's renunciant does the required work without leaning on its fruit; giving up the ritual fire is not enough. Next, Krishna will explain what it means to act without leaning on the fruit.

verses.sa: यं संन्यासमिति प्राहुर्योगं तं विद्धि पाण्डव । न ह्यसंन्यस्तसङ्कल्पो योगी भवति कश्चन ॥
verses.tr: Arjuna, what people call renunciation is yoga. No one becomes a yogi without giving up intentions.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna asks Arjuna to listen for one Sanskrit word that shows exactly why a person cannot become a yogi.

body.text: Arjuna, what people call renunciation is yoga. No one becomes a yogi without giving up intentions. The word sankalpa, intention, is the only inner obstacle to becoming a yogi. Krishna says that without dropping these inner intentions, no one becomes a yogi, and true renunciation is simply giving up these intentions. Krishna now explains that action is the way up, but stillness is the way to stay there.

verses.sa: आरुरुक्षोर्मुनेर्योगं कर्म कारणमुच्यते । योगारूढस्य तस्यैव शमः कारणमुच्यते ॥
verses.tr: For the sage who seeks to rise into yoga, action is the means. For the one who has risen in yoga, stillness is the means.
verses.angle: Action and stillness as two causes
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna shifts from what renunciation is to how to practice it. He now divides the path into two stages, and names the tool for each.

body.text: For the sage who seeks to rise into yoga, action is the means. For the one who has risen in yoga, stillness is the means. Notice how the word karanam, cause, is used for both stages, yet the tool changes. For the one seeking to rise, action is the cause, and for the one who has risen, stillness is the cause. Krishna next describes the person who has let go of sense pleasures and actions entirely.

verses.sa: यदा हि नेन्द्रियार्थेषु न कर्मस्वनुषज्जते । सर्वसङ्कल्पसंन्यासी योगारूढस्तदोच्यते ॥
verses.tr: When one no longer clings to sense pleasures or to actions, that person is called established in yoga, having renounced all intentions.
verses.angle: yogarudha: the one mounted on yoga
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna now tells Arjuna how to know he has reached that height. Listen for the state of the mind that is no longer caught.

body.text: When one no longer clings to sense pleasures or to actions, that person is called established in yoga, having renounced all intentions. The key word is yogarudhah, one mounted on yoga. The verse shows that this is the state of a person who does not cling to sense objects or to actions, because he has renounced all intentions. Krishna then turns to how the self must lift itself up without letting itself fall.

verses.sa: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
verses.tr: Lift yourself by yourself; do not let yourself fall. The true self is its own friend, and the true self is its own enemy.
verses.angle: Atmanah: the self as its own friend and enemy
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: If yoga is a state of peace, what breaks that peace? Krishna asks Arjuna to look inside, because the enemy is not out there.

body.text: Lift yourself by yourself; do not let yourself fall. The true self is its own friend, and the true self is its own enemy. The word is atmanah, of the self. The self is its own friend and its own enemy. The same self that saves you can also destroy you. Krishna now shows the exact way the higher self acts as a friend, and the lower self acts as an enemy.

verses.sa: बन्धुरात्माऽऽत्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः । अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत् ॥
verses.tr: For one who has conquered the lower self by the true self, the true self is a friend. For one who has not conquered the lower self, the true self behaves like an enemy.
verses.angle: The self is friend or enemy
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna asks how one can be a friend to oneself. Listen to how he defines the inner battle.

body.text: For one who has conquered the lower self by the true self, the true self is a friend. For one who has not conquered the lower self, the true self behaves like an enemy. The word atma is used twice in one breath. The true self is a friend only when the lower self, the restless mind, is conquered by the true self. Without that victory, the self itself becomes the enemy. Krishna says that for the one who has conquered the self, the supreme reality is present in heat and cold, pleasure and pain.

verses.sa: जितात्मनः प्रशान्तस्य परमात्मा समाहितः । शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु तथा मानापमानयोः ॥
verses.tr: For one who has conquered the self and is serene, the supreme reality is ever present in heat and cold, pleasure and pain, honor and dishonor.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna states that the Supreme Reality is present to the self-conquered. Listen for the pairs of opposites that frame this state.

body.text: For one who has conquered the self and is serene, the supreme reality is ever present in heat and cold, pleasure and pain, honor and dishonor. The word is manaapamaanayo, honor and insult. The supreme reality is present to the self-conquered person, whether they experience praise or blame. Krishna says that person is called a yogi because they see clay, stone, and gold as the same.

verses.sa: ज्ञानविज्ञानतृप्तात्मा कूटस्थो विजितेन्द्रियः । युक्त इत्युच्यते योगी समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः ॥
verses.tr: One whose mind is satisfied by knowledge and realization, who remains steady, who has conquered the senses, and who sees clay, stone, and gold alike is called a yogi in union.
verses.angle: Samaloshtashmakanchanah: equal in clay, stone, and gold
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Arjuna is still learning how to stand firm without being pulled by fear or desire. Listen to how Krishna names the one who is satisfied by understanding.

body.text: One whose mind is satisfied by knowledge and realization, who remains steady, who has conquered the senses, and who sees clay, stone, and gold alike is called a yogi in union. Listen to one compound, samaloshtashmakanchanah. It means equal in clay, stone, and gold. The yogi does not rank the world by greed. Krishna now adds another sign of the one who stands firm, equal to friend and enemy.

verses.tr: The one whose understanding is equal toward friend, enemy, neutral person, mediator, hateful person, relative, the virtuous, and the sinful is श्रेष्ठ.
verses.angle: Equal understanding toward every type of person
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: In the last verse Krishna spoke of seeing clay, stone, and gold with the same eye. Now he speaks of seeing people.

body.text: The one whose understanding is equal toward friend, enemy, neutral person, mediator, hateful person, relative, the virtuous, and the sinful is श्रेष्ठ. Friend, enemy, neutral, relative, saint or sinner: whoever sees them with an even mind stands out among yogis. Next he turns from people to the yogi's own place of dwelling, asking him to sit alone and fix his mind on the supreme.

verses.sa: योगी युञ्जीत सततमात्मानं रहसि स्थितः । एकाकी यतचित्तात्मा निराशीरपरिग्रहः ॥
verses.tr: The disciplined yogi, dwelling alone in seclusion, should constantly unite the mind with the supreme being, free from desire and possessiveness, with body and mind under control.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just described the yogi who sees everyone equally. Now he tells the yogi what to actually do. Listen for the conditions the yogi must create.

body.text: The disciplined yogi, dwelling alone in seclusion, should constantly unite the mind with the supreme being, free from desire and possessiveness, with body and mind under control. Notice the word nirashiraparigrahah, without desire and possessiveness. Krishna is not asking for a feeling of emptiness, but for the removal of attachment to results and things. He tells the yogi to find a clean spot and set up a firm seat. But where is this seat placed?

verses.sa: शुचौ देशे प्रतिष्ठाप्य स्थिरमासनमात्मनः । नात्युच्छ्रितं नातिनीचं चैलाजिनकुशोत्तरम् ॥
verses.tr: Having placed a firm seat for himself on a clean spot, neither too high nor too low, with cloth, deerskin, and kusha grass laid in layers.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna describes the physical setup for meditation, a simple seat on clean ground. Listen for the exact material details.

body.text: Having placed a firm seat for himself on a clean spot, neither too high nor too low, with cloth, deerskin, and kusha grass laid in layers. The verse uses the word na atyucchritam, meaning not too high, to describe the height of the seat. A seat that is not too high keeps the body steady and the mind from wandering. Sitting on that seat, the yogi must make the mind one-pointed and restrain its movements to begin the practice of yoga.

verses.sa: तत्रैकाग्रं मनः कृत्वा यतचित्तेन्द्रियक्रियः । उपविश्यासने युञ्ज्याद्योगमात्मविशुद्धये ॥
verses.tr: Sitting on that seat, with the mind made one-pointed and the movements of mind and senses restrained, one should practice yoga for inner purification.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna now tells Arjuna to sit down. Listen for the exact state of mind and body he demands before the practice begins.

body.text: Sitting on that seat, with the mind made one-pointed and the movements of mind and senses restrained, one should practice yoga for inner purification. Listen to the long compound word yatacittendriyakriyah. It gathers the mind and the senses into a single act of restraint. This is the condition Krishna sets for the practice. Next, Krishna tells Arjuna to hold the body, head, and neck perfectly still, fixing the gaze on the tip of the nose.

verses.sa: समं कायशिरोग्रीवं धारयन्नचलं स्थिरः । संप्रेक्ष्य नासिकाग्रं स्वं दिशश्चानवलोकयन् ॥
verses.tr: Holding the body, head, and neck straight and still, and gazing only at the tip of the nose without looking around.
verses.angle: samam: holding the body straight and even
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just told Arjuna to sit on the seat and steady the mind. Now He shifts to the body, showing how the posture must match the inner state.

body.text: Holding the body, head, and neck straight and still, and gazing only at the tip of the nose without looking around. The word samam means holding the body straight and even. It is a rule of balance, because the body is held straight so the mind can become steady. With the body still, Krishna now tells the yogi to fix the mind on Him and sit devoted to the Supreme.
